First chair

Michele De Lucchi’s chair for Memphis: a metal hoop that carries a blue disc and two black balls.

Source
National Gallery of Victoria: First, chair (D75-1985)
Creator
Michele De Lucchi (designer); Memphis, Milan (manufacturer and retailer)
Made
1983
Style
Memphis (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Playful, graphic, light, postmodern
Evidence
Downloaded the museum’s published image (694 × 859 px) from the National Gallery of Victoria to a private scratchpad and inspected it with the Read tool on 2026-09-25. No image is stored in the catalogue. The Met record was also read; it has no online image.
Reviewed
25 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The NGV lists De Lucchi as designer and Memphis, Milan, as manufacturer and retailer; lacquered metal and wood, 90.3 × 66.2 × 46.2 cm, purchased in 1985. NGV record.

The Met describes a black wooden seat disc on four tubular legs, with a tilted tubular hoop that carries a turquoise disc backrest and two black ball armrests. It calls the chair characteristic of the Memphis collective that De Lucchi co-founded with Sottsass. Met record, accession 2021.54.10.

Observed

  • A gray tubular ring rises from the front legs and tilts back behind the seat.
  • A flat blue disc is fixed at the top of the ring as the backrest.
  • Two glossy black spheres sit on the ring at the sides as armrests.
  • The round seat is black, on four thin straight gray legs.

Why it belongs

The chair is drawn with lines and dots: a circle, a disc, and two balls. It shows that Memphis could be sparse. Here the play comes from geometry and a few colors, not from pattern.

Borrow

Compose with a thin circular line and a few solid dots placed on it.

Let one saturated disc of color act as the focal point against black and gray.
